name: Why Redux Toolkit exists
description: Redux Toolkit (RTK) is the official, recommended way to write Redux logic. It was created to address common complaints about classic Redux — too much boilerplate, too many packages to configure, and easy-to-make mutation mistakes — by bundling sensible defaults and utilities like createSlice, configureStore, and Immer.
notes: The Redux docs now consider hand-written createStore/combineReducers/switch-reducer code a legacy pattern; RTK is the standard for new projects.

name: createReducer()
description: A Redux Toolkit utility for writing a reducer as a map of action types to case reducer functions (using a builder callback) instead of a switch statement, with Immer-powered 'mutating' update syntax.
parameters: initialState — the reducer's default state. builder — object with addCase(), addMatcher(), and addDefaultCase() methods to register handlers.
returns: A reducer function suitable for combineReducers or configureStore.
notes: createSlice uses createReducer internally — most apps use createSlice directly rather than calling createReducer standalone.

name: Immer immutability in RTK
description: Redux Toolkit uses the Immer library internally so that code written inside createSlice/createReducer can 'mutate' a draft state object using normal JavaScript syntax, while Immer produces a correctly immutable next state behind the scenes.
example:
// Inside a slice reducer, this is safe and produces an immutable update:
state.todos.push(newTodo);
notes: Immer only applies inside RTK's reducer builders — plain hand-written reducers outside createSlice/createReducer still must not mutate state.

name: RTK Query overview
description: RTK Query is a data-fetching and caching layer built into Redux Toolkit. It generates hooks like useGetTodosQuery from an API definition, automatically handling loading/error state, caching, re-fetching, and cache invalidation without hand-written thunks or reducers.
notes: RTK Query is often described as eliminating the need to hand-write data-fetching thunks, reducers, and selectors for server state.

name: createEntityAdapter()
description: A Redux Toolkit utility that generates a set of prebuilt reducers and selectors for managing a normalized collection of items (keyed by id) in a slice, such as adding, updating, and removing entities.
parameters: selectId — optional function to extract an item's id. sortComparer — optional function to keep the collection sorted.
returns: An adapter object with getInitialState(), reducer methods (addOne, updateOne, removeOne, etc.), and getSelectors().
notes: Normalizing collections by id avoids deeply nested/duplicated data and makes lookups O(1).

name: Matcher utilities (isPending, isFulfilled, isRejected)
description: Redux Toolkit ships matcher functions that identify action types generated by any createAsyncThunk (or a specific one), for use with extraReducers' addMatcher to handle loading/success/error state generically across multiple thunks.
parameters: isPending / isFulfilled / isRejected — matcher functions, usable standalone or scoped to specific thunks via isPending(thunkA, thunkB).
example:
import { isPending } from '@reduxjs/toolkit';
builder.addMatcher(isPending, (state) => { state.loading = true; });
notes: Useful for a shared 'any request is loading' flag without listing every thunk's pending case individually.

name: createListenerMiddleware()
description: A Redux Toolkit middleware for running side-effect logic in response to dispatched actions or state changes, as a lighter-weight alternative to redux-saga for reactive async workflows.
returns: A middleware instance with a `.startListening()` method to register listeners and a `.middleware` to add to the store.
notes: Added in newer versions of Redux Toolkit as a built-in alternative to reaching for redux-saga or redux-observable for simpler cases.

name: Redux DevTools integration
description: configureStore automatically wires up the Redux DevTools browser extension in development, enabling action logging, state diffing, and time-travel debugging with zero manual setup.
notes: In classic Redux this required manually composing `window.__REDUX_DEVTOOLS_EXTENSION_COMPOSE__` with your store enhancers.

name: Default middleware in RTK
description: configureStore automatically includes redux-thunk for async logic plus development-only middleware that warns on state mutations and non-serializable values placed in actions or state.
notes: Use getDefaultMiddleware() and .concat()/.prepend() to add custom middleware without losing the built-in checks.

name: PayloadAction<T> (TypeScript)
description: A generic type Redux Toolkit provides for typing the action objects passed into slice reducers, so `action.payload` has a concrete type instead of `any` in TypeScript projects.
notes: Without PayloadAction, TypeScript infers action.payload as unknown/any inside createSlice reducers.
